biological.citation: kcnb1 loss of function in zebrafish causes neurodevelopmental and epileptic disorders associated with γ-aminobutyric acid dysregulation (PMID: 40332468)
biological.summary: In wild-type larval zebrafish, kcnb1 was expressed in various regions of the central nervous system including neurons, oligodendrocytes, and microglial cells. Both kcnb1+/- and kcnb1-/- zebrafish displayed impaired swimming behavior and epilepsy-like features restored by human Kv2.1 WT DNA. The kcnb1-/- model showed spontaneous and provoked epileptiform-like electrographic activity associated with GABA dysregulation, with increased bdnf mRNA and c-Fos fluorescence in the telencephalon upon PTZ exposure.

biological.citation: Epilepsy and neurobehavioral abnormalities in mice with a dominant-negative KCNB1 pathogenic variant (PMID: 33132203)
biological.summary: The KCNB1-p.G379R variant was shown to have a dominant-negative effect on KV2.1 clustering at endoplasmic reticulum-plasma membrane junctions in HEK293T cells. Kcnb1G379R knock-in mice exhibited spontaneous seizures, hyperactivity, repetitive behaviors, impulsivity, reduced anxiety, and abnormal interictal EEG activity. Immunohistochemistry revealed genotype-dependent reductions in KV2.1, KV2.2, and AMIGO-1 protein expression, confirming both conducting and non-conducting (structural) roles of KCNB1.

biological.citation: Integrin-KCNB1 potassium channel complexes regulate neocortical neuronal development and are implicated in epilepsy (PMID: 36207442)
biological.summary: KCNB1 forms complexes with integrins α5β5 (Integrin-K+ channel Complexes, IKCs) in neocortical neurons, and biochemical signaling of these complexes was impaired in Kcnb1-R312H knock-in mice. KCNB1 null mice showed impaired neuronal migration of glutamatergic neurons, disrupted morphology, synaptic connectivity defects, seizures, anxiety, and compulsive behavior. Treatment with Angiotensin II (a Focal Adhesion kinase agonist) in vitro corrected the neuronal abnormalities, demonstrating a non-conducting developmental role for KCNB1 via IKC signaling.

biological.citation: KCNB1-Leptin receptor complexes couple electric and endocrine function in the melanocortin neurons of the hypothalamus (PMID: 39436109)
biological.summary: KCNB1 (Kv2.1) forms stable complexes with the leptin receptor (LepR) in hypothalamic neurons including POMC-expressing neurons of the Arcuate nucleus. Mice lacking functional KCNB1 channels had less adipose tissue, lower circulating leptin, insensitivity to leptin-induced anorexia, and aberrant POMC production. Canonical LepR-STAT3 signaling was impaired while non-canonical PI3K/Akt/FOXO1 and ERK signaling were constitutively upregulated, establishing KCNB1 as a molecular link between neuronal excitability and endocrine function.

biological.citation: Functions and clinical significance of KCNB1 in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 39893596)
biological.summary: siRNA knockdown of KCNB1 in human ESCC cell lines (KYSE70 and TE5) inhibited cell proliferation, G2-M phase progression, migration, and invasion, and induced apoptosis. Microarray analysis showed KCNB1 regulates Ephrin receptor signaling by suppressing EPHB1, EPHB2, and ERK1/2 gene expression. Immunohistochemical analysis of 129 primary ESCC tumor samples identified high KCNB1 expression as an independent prognostic factor for poor 5-year relapse-free survival.

biological.citation: Antagonistic roles of Ras-MAPK and Akt signaling in integrin-K(+) channel complex-mediated cellular apoptosis (PMID: 35357039)
biological.summary: In response to oxidative stress, IKCs (complexes of α5-integrins and KCNB1/Kv2.1) activate an apoptotic Ras-MAPK/ERK signaling pathway. Simultaneously, wild-type KCNB1 channels sequester Akt, causing dephosphorylation of BAD and promoting apoptosis, whereas the C73A KCNB1 variant that does not induce apoptosis does not sequester Akt. These findings place KCNB1 at the intersection of pro-apoptotic Ras-MAPK and pro-survival Akt signaling pathways.

biological.citation: Spectrum of K(V) 2.1 Dysfunction in KCNB1-Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorders (PMID: 31600826)
biological.summary: High-throughput functional screening of 17 KCNB1 variants associated with DEE or other NDDs revealed diverse molecular defects including altered current density, shifts in voltage dependence of activation/inactivation, reduced total KV2.1 expression, and deficient cell-surface expression. Pathogenic variants exhibited these defects both as homotetramers and when co-expressed with wild-type KV2.1. This established a platform for rapid screening of KV2.1 functional defects and demonstrated that KCNB1 variants cause dysfunction through multiple distinct mechanisms.

biological.citation: Gain-of-function enhancer variant near KCNB1 causes familial ST-depression syndrome (PMID: 40208226)
biological.summary: A rare non-coding variant located 18 kb downstream of KCNB1 on chromosome 20 was identified in all affected individuals across 20 families with familial ST-depression syndrome (FSTD), with full penetrance and autosomal dominant inheritance. The variant creates a MEF2-binding site that enhances transcriptional activity, and 4C chromosome conformation capture confirmed direct interaction between this locus and the KCNB1 promoter in AC16 cardiomyocytes and human muscle tissue. dCas9-activator/repressor assays showed KCNB1 was the only gene consistently regulated by the locus, implicating KCNB1 for the first time in human cardiac electrophysiology and arrhythmogenesis.

biological.citation: Role of KCNB1 in the prognosis of gliomas and autophagy modulation (PMID: 28144039)
biological.summary: KCNB1 expression was associated with favorable overall survival and progression-free survival in glioma patients across three datasets (CGGA, GSE16011, REMBRANDT). In vitro studies showed KCNB1 induces autophagy accompanied by increased apoptosis and reduced proliferation and invasion of glioma cells via the ERK pathway, confirmed by inhibition with a selective ERK1/2 inhibitor (U0126) or siERK1/2. In vivo studies confirmed KCNB1-induced autophagy inhibited tumor growth and increased survival.

biological.citation: ASHG 2016 - Genetic variants in KCNB1 are modestly associated with type 2 diabetes in American Indians from the Gila River Indian Community
biological.summary: An intronic 16 bp deletion in KCNB1 (MAF=0.02) was associated with protection from type 2 diabetes in 7,351 Pima Indians (OR=0.51, p=1.2×10⁻³). A common variant rs3827088 (MAF=0.31) was also nominally associated with T2D and replicated in an independent cohort of 3,004 American Indians (combined N=10,448, OR=1.18, p=2.5×10⁻⁴). Conditional analysis suggested the two variants have independent effects on T2D risk, consistent with KCNB1's known role in regulating insulin secretion.
